engine_note: Cyberpunk mods are NOT 'one folder into Mods/'. A single archive scatters files across archive/pc/mod, mods/, bin/x64/plugins, r6/scripts and red4ext. root_merge therefore installs FILE BY FILE, journals every target path, and backs up any file it is about to overwrite. It never touches archive/pc/content, archive/pc/ep1, engine/ or the game executables.

identity.name: Cyberpunk 2077
identity.note: AppID 1091500. Proton (Windows build), but every path this plugin writes is INSIDE the game folder, never in the Proton prefix. Framework installers (CET/RED4ext/ArchiveXL) are user-managed: this plugin only drops their files, it never runs an .exe/installer.

paths.write_roots_note: Every install target must be under one of these. archive/pc/mod is the classic .archive drop; mods/ is REDmod; bin/x64/plugins is Cyber Engine Tweaks; r6/scripts is redscript; red4ext is the RED4ext plugin loader. A file whose target is not covered is REJECTED, never written elsewhere.
paths.protected_note: Original game payload. A mod that wants to write here is either a patch tool (not a mod) or trying to replace shipped data; both are refused. Overwriting a file that already exists inside a write root is allowed ONLY with a backup recorded in the journal.
notes: Cyberpunk has no game-managed mod list file: a mod is present because its files are present. state_file/state_staging are null and all state-file preflight/snapshot/drift logic is skipped, exactly like SMAPI.
staging and quarantine sit on the SAME filesystem as GAME_ROOT so os.replace() never hits EXDEV(18).

loaders_note: Listing a loader does NOT mean this plugin installs it. Users install CET/RED4ext/ArchiveXL themselves; a mod that needs them shows a dependency note.

mod_package.manifest_note: Only REDmod packages carry info.json (name/version). Classic .archive drops have no manifest at all, so the package id is derived from the archive name and the file set, never from a guessed UniqueID.

import_roots.label: downloads
import_roots.note: Where the Game Mode browser saves files. READ ONLY: nothing here is ever created, moved or deleted.

import_roots_note: Same contract as the SMAPI descriptor: the inbox stays first, this is a read-only courtesy so a mod downloaded in the browser can be imported.
capabilities_note: enable_disable=false on purpose: Cyberpunk has no on/off switch for a dropped .archive. Claiming it would produce a button that silently does nothing. uninstall_quarantine=true because every install is journaled per FILE, so removal is exact and reversible.

download_sources.note: Nexus is browsed in the signed-in browser; downloads land in ~/Downloads and are imported from there. No API key is used. Round 78: nexus_game_domain is the BROWSE-ONLY alias — the three website-page openers (open_mod_page / open_search_page / open_browse_page) read it, while the API RPCs (nexus_recent/nexus_mod/nexus_download_link) still require a nexus_metadata block and a stored key.

safety.note: An install that would replace an existing file records a byte-exact backup first. Uninstall restores it; a rollback restores it too.

known_limitations: Framework installers (CET, RED4ext, ArchiveXL, redscript) must be installed by the user; this plugin only drops their files.
No load order: Cyberpunk resolves archives by name, so two mods editing the same record still conflict and the game decides.
REDmod packages are detected but not compiled; run `redmod` yourself if a mod ships uncompiled scripts.
